title: Terry Fox: Greatest Canadian Hero
summary: Hosts Josh and Chuck profile Terry Fox, the Canadian athlete who lost his right leg to osteogenic sarcoma at 18, then ran his Marathon of Hope across Canada in 1980 on a prosthetic leg to raise money for cancer research. The episode covers his childhood and athletics, his diagnosis and amputation, his prosthetic leg and running style, the start of the run from Newfoundland, media and sponsor support (including the Toronto Star and Leslie Scribner), his cancer returning in his lungs in Thunder Bay which ended the run after 143 days, the 1980 telethon, his death in 1981, his honors, and the annual Terry Fox Run. Also includes a brief preview of an October cruise, a listener email about words that sound like other words in different accents, and sign-off.

segments.title: Canada tour and fan request
segments.summary: Hosts recall their Canadian tour and say listeners asked them to cover Terry Fox; two fans, William the First and Chris, are credited with the suggestion.

segments.title: Stuff at Sea cruise promo
segments.summary: Hosts promote a live show on an October cruise from Brooklyn to Bermuda, booked through Virgin Voyages.

segments.title: Opening banter on Terry Fox
segments.summary: Hosts note Terry Fox's worldwide fame and that he is known for a run across Canada; Josh says he learned of Fox from a 1983 Robert Duvall movie seen on HBO.

segments.title: Early life in Winnipeg and Port Coquitlam
segments.summary: Terry Fox is born in Winnipeg on July 20, 1958, and the family moves to Port Coquitlam near Vancouver.

segments.title: Youth sports and Simon Fraser University
segments.summary: Fox is small but determined in sports, improving from eighth grade to co-athlete of the year, and runs cross country. He attends Simon Fraser University and plays JV basketball; after a car accident and months of knee pain he is diagnosed with cancer in March 1977.

segments.title: Bone cancer and amputation
segments.summary: Fox has osteogenic sarcoma in his knee and his right leg is amputated about six inches above the knee. Hosts discuss the film's handling of this and a Helen Hunt after-school special aside.

segments.title: Wheelchair basketball and training
segments.summary: After chemotherapy, Fox joins the Vancouver Cable Cars wheelchair basketball team, leading it to national tournaments in 1978 and 1979. He meets Rika Noda and trains in his wheelchair on mountain passes.

segments.title: Dick Traum article and motivation
segments.summary: Fox's high school coach gives him an article about Dick Traum, the first amputee to run the New York City Marathon, and Fox decides to run across Canada for cancer research after a doctor says he would have had worse treatment a few years earlier.

segments.title: Prosthetic leg design
segments.summary: Ben Spiker designs a simple nine-pound prosthetic with no shock absorption; Fox runs with a hop-and-skip style. The leg was repaired along the way and three versions are displayed at the Royal British Columbia Museum.

segments.title: First race and early fundraising
segments.summary: Fox enters his first race in August 1979, a 17-mile run, finishing last. He approaches the Canadian Cancer Society, which asks him to first secure corporate sponsors.

segments.title: Corporate sponsors and planning the run
segments.summary: Ford donates a camper van, Adidas donates shoes, and Imperial Oil, Safeway and Pacific Western Airlines help; the run goal is about 7,400 km from St. John's, Newfoundland, to Vancouver. Fox breaks the run into single miles and counts telephone poles.

segments.title: Health concerns and running with mental distraction
segments.summary: Fox gets a certificate of health despite an enlarged heart and dizzy spells; he hides symptoms. Hosts discuss mental endurance in long-distance running.

segments.title: Start of the Marathon of Hope
segments.summary: The run begins April 12, 1980, in Newfoundland with small crowds. The first month raises only about $25,000, and tension grows in the van with Doug Alward.

segments.title: Tensions, brother Darryl, and reception in Quebec
segments.summary: Brother Darryl joins in New Brunswick. Fox gets little publicity or money in Quebec and faces hostile drivers and police removing him from a highway.

segments.title: Toronto Star coverage and national fame
segments.summary: Toronto Star reporter Leslie Scribner writes the column Running with Terry. By Toronto Fox is a national hero, meets Pierre Trudeau, Bobby Orr and Darryl Sittler, and is asked to kick off a football game.

segments.title: Physical toll, press criticism, and Greg Scott
segments.summary: Fox has tendonitis and a dry cough and is overwhelmed by interviews and fundraising demands. Some press criticism follows, including a cheating accusation he got retracted. Ten-year-old amputee Greg Scott wants to ride alongside him.

segments.title: Cancer spreads and run ends in Thunder Bay
segments.summary: After about 3,300 miles Fox feels worse and is hospitalized in Thunder Bay, where the cancer is found in both lungs. He ends the run after 143 days, having averaged 23.3 miles a day and raised about $2 million.

segments.title: 1980 telethon and later fundraising
segments.summary: A September 1980 telethon with Elton John, John Denver, Gordon Lightfoot, Anne Murray and Glen Campbell raises about $10 million more. A later goal of a dollar per Canadian raises about $24.17 million.

segments.title: Death, honors and legacy
segments.summary: Fox dies June 28, 1981, at 22, after pneumonia and a coma. He receives the Companion of the Order of Canada and the Order of the Dogwood, is on postage stamps, and his mother Betty carries the Olympic flag in 2010.

segments.title: Terry Fox Run today
segments.summary: The annual Terry Fox Run takes place on the second Sunday after Labor Day, and the Terry Fox Foundation has reached one billion dollars raised for cancer research.

segments.title: Listener mail on accent wordplay
segments.summary: A listener named Adam shares examples of words that sound like other words in different accents, such as beer can and bacon, and rise up lights and razor blades.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Hosts invite listener email and sign off.
